papers.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
papers.summary: Analyzed six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol anesthesia, and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome to identify a thalamic organization pattern linked to arousability. During N2/N3 sleep, centromedian (CM) and ventral posterolateral (VPL) nuclei showed convergent edge-community profiles and increased closed-loop intra-thalamic motifs, and N3 directed effective connectivity along CM→VPL→pulvinar increased versus wake and N2; stronger CM→VPL and VPL→pulvinar connectivity covaried with higher N3 delta power, which was associated with three-month improvement in behavioral responsiveness in UWS.

papers.title: Multiple platform-induced sleep restriction disrupts time-of-day-dependent corticosterone and leukocyte profiles in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6 mice subjected to subchronic sleep restriction via the multiple-platform procedure, 24-hour diurnal profiles revealed significant time-of-day-dependent differences in serum corticosterone and granulocyte-enriched percentages at specific Zeitgeber times, without altering daily mean corticosterone or total white blood cell counts.

papers.title: Rest promotes microglial clearance of degenerating neurons
papers.summary: Used longitudinal two-photon imaging in mice with cytosolic TDP-43 proteinopathy to show microglia remove neuronal corpses through an ordered reaching-approaching-isolating-digesting sequence. Clearance was higher during the light (resting) phase, reversed with light-dark cycle inversion, and was blunted by sleep disruption; noradrenergic locus coeruleus signaling and ADRB2 acted as a brake on engulfment, while sustained microglial ADRB2 deletion impaired clearance and blunted light-dark differences.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Ecological and integrative physiology
papers.summary: Monitoring locomotor activity in three rodent species and using Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis, the study found robust circadian rhythms in all animals, while infradian rhythms (5- and 10-day ranges) were extremely low in mice and moderate in gerbils and squirrels, with infradian strength less than 10% of circadian strength.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.summary: LogicSleep is a neurosymbolic framework combining a CNN-graph U-Net backbone with Conditional Random Fields and differentiable-logic transition rules for explainable, physiologically plausible, subject-adaptive sleep staging. Across ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 in within- and cross-dataset settings it consistently outperformed strong baselines and improved sequence-level metrics.

papers.title: Effects of pharmacotherapy on quantitative electroencephalogram measures of sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized trial in 16 OSA participants examined quantitative wake EEG during Karolinska Drowsiness Tests after reboxetine alone or combined with oxybutynin versus placebo. No significant treatment effect appeared on slow EEG frequencies or theta/alpha ratio, indicating the agents did not increase neurophysiological markers of next-day sleepiness.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.summary: High-density EEG and spectral/complexity measures characterized eight jhana advanced concentration absorption states in 20 advanced meditators. ACAM-J showed posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all states, and increased entropy-based complexity, with complexity remaining elevated even in late minimal states.

papers.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for sleep disorders in psychiatry.
papers.summary: This chapter reviews neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) for sleep disorders in psychiatric patients, integrating circadian rhythms, sleep homeostasis, neurotransmitter systems, and brain networks with CBT-I, mindfulness, and digital personalization. It argues NIPE is a clinically relevant strategy to improve engagement and sleep outcomes across transdiagnostic psychiatric conditions.

papers.title: Trajectories of Sleep and Pain From the Perioperative Period to One-Year After Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: A prospective cohort of 171 knee arthroplasty patients tracked daily sleep and pain postoperatively and outcomes at one year. Pain and sleep fluctuated bidirectionally in the first postoperative week, and worst-quartile early pain and sleep predicted significantly higher one-year pain; preoperative positive affect explained 13.1% of variance in one-year pain.

papers.title: Longitudinal resting-state EEG-based modeling predicts phenoconversion and delineates heterogeneity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: Applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) modeling to longitudinal resting-state EEG from a prospective cohort of 285 participants with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder to stratify prodromal heterogeneity. Identified a progressive degenerative subtype (delta/theta increases, lower MoCA) and a posterior beta-low subtype, and showed that subtype shifting and accelerated annual stage advancement (ΔStage≥2) identified individuals at exceptionally high phenoconversion risk with survival of 0-15% by 7.5 years.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.summary: Reviews data-driven EEG-fMRI fusion methods published between 2000 and 2025, organizing them by fusion strategy (symmetric vs. asymmetric), methodological objective (factorization vs. translation), and modeling assumptions (linear vs. nonlinear). It reports that no universal validation standard exists and that interpreting latent multimodal components remains difficult, while fusion has revealed distributed network dynamics not accessible through unimodal analyses.

papers.title: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
papers.summary: Proposes a circadian gating of neuroimmune memory framework linking chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction, examining whether circadian context influences formation or expression of neuroimmune memory in microglia. It distinguishes immune memory from ongoing inflammation and specifies experimental tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal while noting that coupling of circadian regulation and innate immune memory in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved.

papers.title: Beyond the RMMA Index: Respiratory-Event Context and Episode Duration in Adults With Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Sleep Bruxism.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed polysomnographic data from 94 adults with OSA and sleep bruxism, matching each of 3774 rhythmic masticatory muscle activity (RMMA) episodes to the nearest respiratory event within a 20 s window. Found that 71.2% of RMMA episodes were temporally related to respiratory events, exceeding chance, with central apnea-related RMMA more likely pre-respiratory or overlapping, and shorter RMMA duration associated with greater respiratory, desaturation, and arousal burden.

papers.title: When impulsivity goes wrong: Circadian timing distinguishes which night shift workers succeed and fail.
papers.summary: Assessed whether phase angle between circadian timing (dim-light melatonin onset, DLMO) and task time predicts impulsivity on the Stop Light Task in 30 night-shift workers. Greater phase angle was associated with worse performance (more crashes) and worse risk strategy, while phase angle did not predict action bias, and post-hoc analysis showed greater sleepiness predicted reduced action bias.

papers.title: Insufficient Sleep, Circadian Targets, Weight Management, and Cardiometabolic Health.
papers.summary: Reviews emerging literature on timing- and circadian-based strategies that may mitigate obesity and cardiometabolic risk in people with habitual insufficient sleep even without increasing sleep duration. Evidence suggests light exposure, food intake, sleep-wake regularity, and physical activity timing influence circadian physiology and metabolic health, but few fully powered randomized trials have directly tested these timing-based pathways, so rigorous trials are needed.

papers.title: Obesity is associated with alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiota in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: Used 16S rRNA gene sequencing of fecal samples from 65 OSA patients and 15 healthy controls to compare gut microbiota according to obesity status. Found altered diversity and composition in OSA, enrichment of Blautia, Fusobacterium, and Eubacterium hallii group with reduced Faecalibacterium, and identified genera such as Acidaminococcus, Megasphaera, and Morganella as characteristic of obese OSA.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional comparison plus a 12-week uncontrolled before-after exercise intervention in permanent night-shift workers, habitually active workers showed greater activity-rest rhythm amplitude, dominant periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization than sedentary workers, with similar pre-to-post changes in the intervention group. Weekend recovery transiently shortened dominant periods to ~18-22 h with acrophase shifts toward diurnal timing, interpreted as adaptive circadian reorganization; the lack of a control group limits causal attribution.

papers.title: Sleep and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Understanding the Bidirectional Relationship.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes clinical, epidemiologic, and neurobiological evidence for a bidirectional relationship between sleep/circadian disturbances and Lewy body disorders, including Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, across prodromal, early, and advanced stages. It highlights proposed mechanisms by which sleep dysfunction may exacerbate neurodegeneration, including impaired proteostasis, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and glymphatic clearance failure.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruptions: Causes, Consequences, and Treatment Approaches.
papers.summary: This review describes circadian rhythms coordinated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus and molecular clock genes (CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, CRY), their modulation by zeitgebers such as light, meal timing, and exercise, and the links between circadian disruption and sleep-wake, metabolic, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, psychiatric, and cancer outcomes. It summarizes assessment approaches (melatonin, questionnaires, sleep diaries, actigraphy) and treatments centered on optimizing light exposure and melatonin to restore circadian alignment.

papers.title: Wearable sensor-based measures on light at day and night, rest-activity circadian rhythm and sleep, and mental health among Hong Kong nurses: a 7-day repeated-measures study.
papers.summary: A 7-day repeated-measures wearable sensor study examined associations of day and night light exposure, rest-activity circadian rhythm, and sleep with mental health among Hong Kong nurses. No abstract was supplied, so specific findings cannot be reported.

papers.title: A changing educational gradient in age-related sleep duration trajectories across birth cohorts.
papers.summary: Using six waves of the China Family Panel Studies (44,379 adults; 134,142 person-wave observations) and hierarchical linear models, this study estimated age and birth-cohort trajectories of sleep duration and their educational gradients. Sleep duration declined with age and was lower in later-born cohorts; higher education was associated with shorter sleep in earlier cohorts, but this educational gradient progressively narrowed across successive cohorts.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial that will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3 sleep-onset chronic insomnia to compare a 12-week Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method intervention against CBT-I, with PSQI change at week 12 as the primary endpoint. Secondary and exploratory endpoints integrate clinical scales, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI/EEG measures of cortical network connectivity to test efficacy and mechanisms.

papers.title: From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a complaint-based clinical framework for identifying, tiered assessing, and integratively managing sleep comorbidities in epilepsy, organizing insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes across life-course and epilepsy-syndrome contexts. The framework links sleep complaints to phenotype recognition, objective testing, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment, but its feasibility and outcome effects remain to be prospectively evaluated.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.summary: Using EEG from 1,534 participants aged 5–21 years during a contrast-change discrimination task, this study combined neural measures of visual response and evidence accumulation with decision modeling to show that perceptual decision accuracy matures earlier than speed. Accuracy improved via fewer attention lapses and more efficient accumulation (half of developmental change by about age 9), whereas non-decision time shortened only between ages 11 and 14, indicating dissociable maturation of decision components.

papers.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
papers.summary: In an observational repeated-measures field study of 19 English Premier League players across 10 European away fixtures, sleep quality dropped on match and subsequent nights versus prematch; overnight stay yielded shorter absolute sleep but a clearer next-night rebound in quality and duration, while immediate return showed no rebound, and match participation moderated sleep duration.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 26,168 pediatric anesthetic records found intraoperative raw EEG use rose from 17.8% to 28.4% over the study period, with wide provider variation (median 18.1%, range 0.9%-79.5%) that case mix explained only weakly (pseudo R2=0.064), indicating individual practice patterns drove uptake.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of central nervous system disease
papers.summary: This RNA-seq study profiled choroid plexus circadian gene expression in a nitroglycerin rat model of chronic migraine versus saline controls and reported sex-specific transcriptomic changes, including upregulated antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) in females and inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8) in males. Circadian genes were dysregulated (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated), with enriched circadian rhythm, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory, lipid metabolism, and heme pathways.

papers.title: SIRT7 Aggravates Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Neuronal Apoptosis via Decreasing Succinylation and Cascaded Ubiquitylation of NFL.
papers.summary: Using a rat chronic sleep deprivation model with hippocampal ubiquitinomics and succinylomics, the study shows SIRT7 desuccinylates neurofilament light (NFL) at K370, suppressing cascaded ubiquitylation and enabling NFL accumulation, which drives cognitive impairment and neuronal apoptosis. SIRT7 inhibition or NFL knockdown attenuated these deficits, implicating SIRT7-NFL succinylation/ubiquitylation in insomnia-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Extreme delta brush as an ictal pattern in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This case report describes a 22-year-old man with anti-NMDAR encephalitis in whom continuous EEG showed extreme delta brush complexes time-locked to stereotyped motor events (right jaw movement and right arm internal rotation), indicating that EDB can be an ictal pattern rather than only a non-ictal biomarker. The case highlights overlap between seizures and dyskinesias and the value of continuous EEG for distinguishing electroclinical seizures from dyskinetic movements.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
papers.summary: In rat models of sleep deprivation, pulpal inflammation and repair were assessed across baseline, LPS-induced pulpitis, and direct pulp capping settings, showing disrupted pulpal homeostasis, impaired hard tissue bridge formation, and later necrosis with apical periodontitis. Transcriptomics and neutrophil analyses implicated enhanced neutrophil accumulation/activation and neutrophil elastase, since neutrophil depletion or NE inhibition (Sivelestat) reduced inflammation and tissue damage.

papers.title: A 6-week vegan Mediterranean diet reduces neutrophil count and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio compared with a traditional Mediterranean diet in women with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial in 25 women with fibromyalgia, a 6-week isocaloric vegan Mediterranean diet significantly reduced neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (P=.026) and neutrophil count (P=.037) compared with a traditional Mediterranean diet, with no between-group differences in kinesiophobia, sleep quality, fatigue, or functional performance.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a girl with a de novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant causing NEDHIB who showed neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia-like nodding episodes, with marked motor and cognitive improvement and complete resolution of nodding after low-dose levodopa-benserazide.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.summary: Holding ATCNet and FBCNet EEG representations fixed, the study tested complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoders across BCI2a, OpenBMI, BCI2b, and BNCI2015-001. SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 pp on BCI2a and 5.470 pp on OpenBMI under cross-entropy-only training, but the advantage attenuated as decoder labels increased; exact-gradient Soft-CLIF also outperformed ANN-SEW, and matched temporal readout largely reduced the differences.

papers.title: The effect of web-based education and therapeutic play methods provided to children undergoing elective surgery on preoperative anxiety and fear, and postoperative pain and sleep: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 78 children aged 7-12 undergoing elective surgery, combining home web-based education with in-hospital therapeutic play significantly reduced preoperative anxiety and fear and postoperative pain versus standard care, but did not improve post-discharge sleep.

papers.title: Suspected Functional Adrenal Insufficiency and Unmasking of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Case for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Restraint.
papers.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Endocrinology and diabetes
papers.summary: This case report describes a man with suspected secondary adrenal insufficiency following migration and night shift work whose symptoms and biochemistry resolved after sleep restoration and nutritional rehabilitation without glucocorticoids, with Hashimoto's thyroiditis unmasked at six-month follow-up.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Comparing 29 iRBD, 24 PD with RBD, 17 PD without RBD, and 18 controls, this study found shared gut dysbiosis (enriched Bifidobacterium, Blautia_A, Azospira_A; reduced Agathobaculum, Clostridium_Q, and others) and decreased fecal butyric and propionic acid in iRBD and PD with RBD, with correlations to clinical severity scales.

papers.title: Circadian orchestration of the cutaneous microenvironment and chronotherapeutic strategies in inflammatory skin diseases.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the circadian mechanisms linking epidermal barrier function and the local immune microenvironment in inflammatory skin diseases (atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, chronic spontaneous urticaria), and proposes a chronotherapeutic framework aligning administration timing of topical agents, systemic drugs, small molecules, and biologics with circadian peaks of their targets. It distinguishes clinically supported timing effects from remaining hypotheses and offers a testable framework for future chronotherapy research.

papers.title: Perioperative methadone: Clinical use and knowledge among Australian anaesthetists.
papers.summary: A mixed-methods survey and real-time polling study of 726 predominantly Australian anaesthetists characterized perioperative intravenous methadone practice; 50.6% reported using it, with wide variation in dosing strategies and surgical contexts, and 86.1% of users co-administered additional opioids or CNS depressants. Polling revealed variability in interpreting pharmacological principles, especially timing of central effects, highlighting targets for education and institutional safeguards.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
papers.summary: This narrative review of 39 studies synthesized evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, risk perception, self-efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 behaviors among emerging adults (18-29 years) using the Health Belief Model. It found knowledge alone appeared insufficient for sustained health behaviors, risk was frequently underestimated, and self-efficacy may translate awareness into behavior, informing a proposed framework requiring empirical testing.

papers.title: Atypical delusional misidentification with alternating impostors in a single body: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 42-year-old woman with persecutory and grandiose delusions who believed different individuals alternately inhabited her husband's unchanged body, expressing full conviction without insight despite unremarkable neurological and routine laboratory findings. The presentation shares features with Capgras and Fregoli syndromes but fits neither, suggesting disturbed continuity of perceived personal identity rather than facial recognition alone.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
